Alice M.: heads up, I saw a perf regression on nightly after the kernel-selector change.  p50 for small-chat doubled on P4s for some sequences. :frowning:
Ben P.: hmm. which selector condition fired? the new seq-length-first branch?
Alice M.: yeah selector now prefers flash-variant-alpha for seq<=256, fuse-kern for <=512, paged for >512. seems fine but repro shows fallback to fused at 200 tokens then 700 tokens later it did something weird.
Carol S.: can you paste the perf profile? perfbot usually captures kernel times.
Eve (perfbot): profile attached (summary): flash-alpha: 4.2ms, fused: 8.1ms, paged: 6.4ms. KV-copy overhead increased by ~2.5ms when fused was used with interleaved layout.
Devon K.: interleaved layout? did we switch to interleaved by default last week for reduced memcpy?
Ben P.: yes, default layout rolled in with CL 4521. It's: [B, T, Hk] interleaved in memory for faster matmul packing.
Alice M.: stack trace from gpu profiler:
```
FlashKernel::forward 4.2ms
FusedAttn::forward 8.1ms
KVBuffer::gather (memcpy) 2.8ms
```
Carol S.: memory copy looks suspicious. interleaved layout may misalign KV stride for fused kernel's gather codepath — fused assumes separate contiguous K and V planes with 128-byte alignment.
Devon K.: avx/cuda kernels expect 128B alignment for coalesced loads. interleaving with dtype=bf16 gives stride that isn't a multiple of 128 for certain head sizes (e.g., 46 heads).
Ben P.: reproduce case: bs=4, seq=200 then extend to 700, heads=46, head_dim=64, dtype=bf16. fused kernel decides to use packed gather with fast path but fails alignment -> falls back to memcpy -> perf hits.
Alice M.: here's a minimal repro command we used on p4d:
```
python bench_attn.py --model-style=open --bs 4 --seq 700 --heads 46 --head-dim 64 --dtype bf16
```
Eve (perfbot): regression delta: +2.6ms p50, +4.9ms p95 on nightly compared to yesterday.
Carol S.: quick idea: selector should consider (heads * head_dim * bytes_per_elem) % 128 == 0 as a condition to pick fused safely. otherwise prefer flash-paged or flash-alpha.
Devon K.: agree. or alter fused gather to handle unaligned strides without memcpy (vectorized unaligned loads). but that's intrusive.
Ben P.: smaller change: add layout predicate into kernel selection heuristics: allow_fused = aligned && seq_in_range && dtype_ok. That should be fast to implement.
Alice M.: will that help batching heuristics? recall batching packs sequences with pad trimming; mixed seq batches may produce effective stride variance.
Carol S.: good point. batching groups with dynamic bucketing by seq length; if within bucket we still have mixed head alignment from model parallel partitions, it could still break. but we can compute effective stride at runtime per batch before kernel pick.
Devon K.: runtime check cost is negligible (a few integer ops). implement check in batch_sched: compute stride = head_count * head_dim * bytes(dtype) and check alignment.
Ben P.: also add telemetry event: kernel_choice_reason = {seq_len:, batch_sz:, stride_aligned: true/false, chosen_kernel:}. Assign to perf logs so we can aggregate.
Alice M.: I ran a quick patch that adds the alignment predicate and forces fallback to flash-paged when unaligned. results on local P4: p50 back to baseline, p95 slightly improved. no correctness issues.
Eve (perfbot): test run results: with alignment-gate enabled: flash-selected 67% of batches, flash-paged 28%, fused 5% (only for perfectly aligned batches). overall tokens/sec +9%.
Carol S.: follow-ups:
- Ben: push selector patch + telemetry as PR.
- Devon: file an infra issue to document alignment constraints for fused kernels (and add warnings in kernel docs).
- Alice: add unit test that constructs odd-head counts and asserts selector avoids fused.
Ben P.: working on branch. small API change: KernelSelector::can_use_fused(batch) -> bool. Will add tests and perf telemetry tag.
Devon K.: long term, we should explore a packed-interleaved fused kernel variant that supports arbitrary strides without memcpy. But that needs kernel rewrite and more validation.
Alice M.: agreed, but do short-term fix first. I've marked the regression incident as mitigated in monitoring (reverted selector to older branch) until PR lands. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy queued for candidate-selector-fix on canary cluster.
Ben P.: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9123
Carol S.: nice work. once PR merges, let's run canary for 24h and then promote.
Alice M.: thanks all. I'll close this thread after canary passes. For the record: root cause = fused kernel assumptions + interleaved bf16 layout causing unaligned KV strides -> memcpy fallback -> perf regression.
